subject: other possible NaN fixes due to conflict in data/constraints

messages.author: cc7570824c8ba017
messages.subject: other possible NaN fixes due to conflict in data/constraints
parts:
Hi BioGeoBEARS group,

I know this has been addressed, but during a constrained analysis I am getting NaNs. I have tried adjusting the time periods as much as I can without betraying geological history, manually created state lists for each time slice to substitute for areas allowed matrices, and reviewed both for conflicts with existing ranges. 

The NaNs are thrown only on certain external nodes so I am wondering if they matter since the tips have extant ranges, maybe I'm confused here though. I also exclude disjunct areas (eg. ABE not allowed) and perhaps this is creating the problem? Any insight would be greatly appreciated!

Best,
Chauncey

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] other possible NaN fixes due to conflict in data/constraints
parts:
Hi, 

The NaNs do matter, they probably mean you have set up constraints that make your data impossible (likelihood=0, log-likelihood=-Infinity).

The thing to think about is whether there is a viable series of transitions between your different tips.  E.g. if you had a tip with ABCD but you had excluded ABC, ACD, and BCD from the state space, there would be no way to get to ABCD from any other state.

Main advice: constrain the state space less.

Cheers,
Nick
